thread:
incident-bot: ALERT — latency SLO breach detected on cont-batch serving pool us-west-2-prod (p99 > 1.6s). Auto-paging oncall.
Mira (oncall): on it, pulling metrics. seeing p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.9s for streaming endpoints. spike started ~ 11:47 UTC.
Jake (runtime): noticed a rise in batch sizes and KV cache churn in the cont-batch path around 11:46. Mixed sequence-length workload spiking packing heuristics.
Sara (sre): is customer impact known? any 5xxs or partial streams?
Lewis (cust-success): AcmePay reports intermittent partial streaming responses in their dashboard — about 8% of requests retried by client. They just escalated.
Mira (oncall): logs show increased serialization stalls in streaming worker logs: `stall_ms=1200` repeated, and `pack_wait_ms` bump from median 12 -> 240.
Jake (runtime): hypothesis: continuous-batching scheduler is favoring large bangs that block stream-y requests (streaming lanes starved). mixed sequence lengths causing greedy packer to inflate latencies.
Mira (oncall): mitigation options?
Jake (runtime): immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) reduce cont_batch.max_size from 96 -> 32 for us-west-2-prod (low-risk config change), 2) enable preferential scheduling for streaming lanes (soft priority), 3) evict old KV entries to reduce cache misses.
Mira (oncall): I'll run 1) and 3) now. applying change to runtime config: 
```
curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/pools/us-west-2-prod/config -d '{"cont_batch":{"max_size":32}}'
```
Sara (sre): I'm flipping traffic policy to route streaming requests to the dedicated streaming pool as fallback for 5% of traffic (canary). command: `route set --pool=us-west-2-stream-dedicated --weight=5%`
Mira (oncall): KV eviction job kicked: `evict_kv --pool=us-west-2-prod --age=10m` — running.
incident-bot: NOTE — config change applied (cont_batch.max_size=32) at 11:55:02 UTC by Mira (oncall).
Mira (oncall): early telemetry: p99 dropped from 1.9s -> 1.1s within 60s after change. pack_wait_ms tail reduced. p95 now ~ 360ms.
Lewis (cust-success): telling AcmePay we have mitigation in place; asking if they still see partial streams. will update.
Jake (runtime): need post-fix follow-ups: 1) tune packer scoring to account for streaming flag and seq_len variance, 2) experiment with per-tenant batch caps, 3) add metric for `stream_preempt_count` and `long_pack_wait_ratio`.
Sara (sre): we should also add an alert for pack_wait_ms p95>200ms. current SLO didn't cover packing stalls explicitly.
Mira (oncall): agree. raising an incident page to eng-runtime for root cause + long-term fix. tagging Jake.
Jake (runtime): I'll own the RCA. initial plan: reproduce with mixed seq-length generator (10% long sequences) and run the packer with current heuristic; explore greedy->fair-share scheduling.
Mira (oncall): customer impact summary for postmortem: AcmePay experienced ~8% partial stream retries for ~9 minutes, p99 breach to ~1.9s, no 5xxs. mitigation applied in ~8 minutes to bring p99 to ~1.1s.
Lewis (cust-success): communicated timeline to AcmePay; they asked for SLA credit if recurring. I'll capture their logs and follow up.
Sara (sre): creating follow-up ticket: INCIDENT-1719222222-RCA, link to this thread and telemetry graphs.
Mira (oncall): thanks team. leaving the change in place for now while Jake and I run controlled canaries for packer fixes tomorrow. marking incident as mitigated but not closed. :white_check_mark:
Jake (runtime): noted — will post a proposed packer change and perf matrix by EOD tomorrow.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status=mitigated, severity=major, assignees=[Jake (runtime), Mira (oncall)], started=1719222222, mitigated=1719222520.
